text:
B: Hiya! Agnieszka, Wolverhampton.
A: Hello. Martijn. Walthamstow.
B: Ah, you're the engineer with the toilet paper! Abena told me. She was very happy with this.
A: Everyone seems to know. It's a simple test.
B: Simple is the best. My husband would call a man, pay sixty pound, and the man does the toilet paper. [laughs]
A: Probably. What do you do?
B: School office, primary school. Front desk, attendance, dinner money. And now dinner money is on new app, so all the parents ring me to ask how is the app working. I don't know also.
A: Who chose the app?
B: The trust. Nobody asked us.
A: That's usually how it works. You're from Poland?
B: Łódź. Eighteen years here. You are Dutch, yeah? Sana said.
A: Dordrecht. Twenty-three years. I came for two.
B: [laughs] Everybody says this! Two years. My husband said also, two years, we save money, we go back. Now my kids are English.
A: Do you think about going back?
B: Sometimes. My mum is in Łódź, seventy-eight, alone. I think, I go back or I bring her here. But my daughter is doing A-levels, my son is in Leeds. Is not simple.
A: No. Er, my father died when I was thirty-eight. I didn't get back in time. It was very fast.
B: Oh. I'm sorry. That is my big fear, honestly.
A: I'm not saying it to frighten you. Just, if you're thinking about it, think about it now. Not later.
B: Yeah. No, you're right. Thank you for saying. Is not easy to say that to a stranger.
A: It's easier with a stranger. [pause] Do you go back often?
B: Once, twice a year. I drive sometimes, two days. I don't mind. Podcasts, coffee, is fine.
A: I take the train. Eurostar, then to Rotterdam. Better than airports.
B: Good. You miss Dutch food?
A: The bread. British bread is too soft. Like a sponge.
B: Yes! Thank you! There's a Polish shop on Dudley Road, proper bread, heavy, with seeds. If you lived in Wolverhampton I would tell you go there.
A: Walthamstow has some Polish shops. I hadn't thought of it. I'll look.
B: Rye bread. Is the best. Your daughter likes Dutch things?
A: Hagelslag. Chocolate sprinkles on bread. She's fourteen, she complains about everything else.
B: [laughs] Mine is seventeen. She complains also, but now sometimes she cooks with me. Is coming back slowly.
A: Everyone keeps telling me that. Joanne said they come round if you keep turning up.
B: She is right. You keep turning up. That's all.
